s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges and unstructured whitish areas
salient_findings: Painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
Verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges
Unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis on dermoscopy
key_facts: 60-year-old patient with no significant medical history
3-year history of macerated skin between toes
18-month history of progressively enlarging ulcer
Received multiple antifungal regimens without improvement
Ulcer measures 3 cm in diameter and extends onto the dorsum of the foot
Hyperkeratotic edges and whitish, fissured base
No palpable popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes
Remainder of examination is unremarkable

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Verrucous, infected ulceration with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Progressively enlarging ulcer with unstructured whitish areas

shortlist.label: Mycetoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, deep-seated infection with possible fungal etiology

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with the lack of response to antifungal treatments, is most consistent with verrucous carcinoma, a type of low-grade malignancy that can resemble a wart and is known for its local destruction and minimal metastatic potential.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the ulcer as verrucous and the lack of lymph node involvement make verrucous carcinoma a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically presents with painful ulcers but does not usually have the verrucous appearance described.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Usually has a more rapid growth phase and often resolves on its own, which does not fit the 18-month progression of the ulcer.

rejected.label: Mycetoma
rejected.why: Involves deeper tissue and typically includes sinus tracts and discharge, not described in this case.
